understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from sitting at the table in silence to holding your ground in it, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being treated as a guest in your own family, and the grief of it, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that their silence is their choice, and their picture is their smallness, not your size.
week_beats.story: A young person who told their truth and was met with silence shows you what holding your ground looks like.

understanding.mirror: You go home for Diwali and sit at the table, but you are a guest in your own family.
understanding.insight: You are the same person who told them the truth and the same person who sat at that table. Their silence is their choice, and their picture is their smallness, not your size.

queries.hook: Being treated as a guest in your own family since you told the truth, and the grief of sitting at the table in silence.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A young person who told their truth and was met with silence, who chose to sit at the table anyway and found their footing in the quiet.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Having seen Krishna's cosmic form, Arjuna realises how casually he treated his closest friend.
verse.sanskrit: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥ यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
verse.line: I treated you casually, as just a friend, never seeing how great you were.
verse.translation: Whatever I said rashly, thinking of you as a friend, 'O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend', not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection, and whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while at play, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in company, I ask your forgiveness for it, immeasurable one.
verse.why: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.

prasang.title: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
prasang.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
prasang.story_hook: Arjuna remembered every joke, every careless 'Hey, Krishna!' across years of friendship, and his voice broke.
prasang.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.

verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

matched.label: My parents' expectations weigh on me

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that it is better to do one's own duty imperfectly than to do another's duty perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous. He says it is better to die in one's own duty than to follow another's path, which is full of fear.
verse.for_you: You cannot live the life your parents wrote for you. It is better to walk your own path, even if it is hard and imperfect, than to sit in their silence and pretend. Your truth is your own duty. Do not borrow a life that was never yours to begin with.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira in the forest. They have lost everything and are waiting for fate to turn. She tells him that no one is saved by passivity. A person must act, even if the path is uncertain. She says never to despise yourself or shrink from your own duty. The one who looks down on themselves finds no real peace or success. It is not about waiting for the world to fix itself. It is about doing what is right and working as if everything depends on your own hands.
verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya defeated and despairing after he has lost his kingdom. She refuses to let him lie there. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for a small, broken life. She urges him to set his mind on something good and stop fearing. He must pull himself together and try again. The past failure does not have to be his final story.
verse.for_you: The silence at the table does not have to be your final story. You are allowed to want more than this quiet room. Your parents' withdrawal is a smallness in them, not a measure of you. Keep your mind on what is truly good for you and stop letting their silence shrink you.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a person who is free inside does not sink in the world. They keep doing whatever work is in front of them. They treat friend and foe the same. They let go of what is lost and take up what comes. They speak gently. They read what is in people's hearts. They do not crave or grieve. They simply live fully in the world while staying calm inside.
verse.for_you: Sit at that table and do the work in front of you. Speak gently, read their silence for what it is, and do not let their quietness pull you under. You will not sink.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the discipline of speech is to say words that cause no distress. They are true, pleasant, and helpful. They are spoken without cruelty. This is how a person stays steady and does not sink in the world.
verse.for_you: When you speak to your parents today, use words that are true but do not wound. Let them hear your truth without the cruelty of blame. This is your discipline.

story.title: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything
story.story_hook: The prince who had everything came back from his travels and stopped laughing.
story.summary: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.
story.lesson: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.

anchor.speaker: Rama's attendant
anchor.setting: Rama's attendants tell King Dasharatha how the prince has changed since his pilgrimage.
anchor.sanskrit: रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो यतःप्रभृति चागतः । सविप्रस्तीर्थयात्रायास्ततःप्रभृति दुर्मनाः ॥
anchor.line: Ever since he came back from the trip, he hasn't been himself.
anchor.translation: Ever since lotus-eyed Rama came back from his pilgrimage with the brahmins, he has been low in spirit.
anchor.why: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.

story.hook_title: Rama came home from his pilgrimage and stopped laughing
story.teaser: Rama came home from his pilgrimage and stopped laughing
story.for_you: They went quiet. You feel like a guest. Rama sat alone too, but he did not stay there. You are not disappearing. You are a person with a life to live. Step out of the silence and find your own ground.

script: They have gone quiet. Not angry, not shouting. Just silent. Since you told them about her, your parents talk to you about the weather. You still go home for Diwali and sit at the table like a guest in your own house. That is a heavy thing to carry.

Arjuna is trembling. He has just seen Krishna's cosmic form. He sees that he took his closest friend for granted. He admits he spoke rashly, treated him as just a friend, and showed disrespect in jest. And Arjuna says: I ask your forgiveness, immeasurable one. Arjuna said:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति, अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि. यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु, एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम्.
In plain words: I treated you casually, as just a friend, never seeing how great you were.

This is what happens when we look at the people we love and we stop truly seeing them. We see them as a friend, a role, or a fixed part of our life. We take their presence for granted. Arjuna is not saying he did not care. He is saying he did not see the full measure of what was right in front of him. It is easy to do this with family. We expect them to always be there, so we stop looking.

Your parents have chosen to see only a version of you. They have not seen the whole of you since you spoke your truth. Their silence is their smallness, not your size. You do not need to shrink to fit the picture they are holding.
You are still the same person who told them the truth.

depth.life: You are sitting at the table during Diwali and you feel like a guest in your own home. The silence from your parents is loud. You told them the truth and now they look at you differently, as if you have shrunk. You go back to the same house and the same table, but the warmth is gone.
depth.points: Arjuna saw the whole universe inside Krishna and realised he had treated him like an ordinary friend. He had not seen the greatness that was right there. The same thing is happening to you. Your parents are looking at you and not seeing who you are.
depth.practice: Sit with your phone and write down one thing you did today that showed who you are, not what they expect.
depth.question: What is one thing you know about yourself that their silence cannot touch?
